text:
ian_k: Heads up — I have a fairly stable repro for a KV-cache paging / page-table corruption issue that shows up with very long contexts (tens of thousands of tokens) on both H100 and A100. Memory keeps growing, pages get evicted but page-table still points at freed slots, leading to stale reads / wrong kv reuse. CC @maria_g @kevin_t

maria_g: Can you paste the minimal repro and exact flags? model, seq len, batch, and whether this is paged-attention or our paged-kv layer? :eyes:

ian_k: Minimal repro and env below. It's our paged-kv path (PagedAttention-style). Observed on llama2-13b-8k + quantized kernels. Run it for ~50k tokens to see the drift.

```
# repro (run on H100 or A100 instances)
python infra/run_repro.py
  --model llama2-13b-8k
  --device gpu
  --gpu-type h100
  --batch 1
  --seq 131072
  --kv-paging enabled
  --page-size 1MB
  --kv-flush-interval 0  # disable automatic flush
```

Logs of interest (trimmed):
```
[1749501.23] kv_page_alloc: page_id=124 ref=1 owner=worker-3
[1749534.87] evict: page_id=124 -> moved to free_list
[1749534.90] page_table_lookup pid=124 -> gpu_ptr=0x7f8a12f000 (stale)
[1749570.11] read_kv: page_id=124 -> WARN: read from stale ptr
[1749600.01] memory_growth: gpu_mem=45.7GB -> 51.3GB
```

kevin_t: I ran this on A100. I see the same pattern — pages show up in the free list but the page_table still maps to old GPU addresses. Profiling with nvprof shows long-lived pinned buffers and lots of small allocations despite eviction. I suspect fragmentation + missing refcount decrements.

ellie_w: Quick dump of our internal page-table instrumentation (increment/decrement counters):
```
pid  inc  dec  active
122  1    1    0
123  1    0    1  <-- leaked dec
124  2    1    1  <-- refcount mismatch when evicted
```

ellie_w: The leak corresponds to a codepath in the fused attention kernel that bails out early for quantized paths. If an exception/fast-exit happens we never call page_release() in that path. Likely introduced when we added the new fused kernel for QKV packing.

perf-bot: Quick perf summary across runs:
- H100: higher page fragmentation, slower compaction cycles, but better raw throughput.
- A100: more frequent OOMs after long-run, slower eviction due to PCIe/GPU driver heuristics.
- Both: memory grows ~5-6 GB after ~40k tokens when kv-flush disabled.

maria_g: Is this a regression? Bisect results?

ian_k: Bisection points to commit abc123def (kv-rework/fused-quant-kernels) as the first bad commit. Prior to that we ran 100k token loops on the same model without leak.

kevin_t: I pushed a local patch that enforces page_release() in the fused kernel exception path and added an assert in the page allocator to check table mappings on evict. Short-term workaround: set `kv-flush-interval=4096` to force periodic full flush which keeps GPU memory bounded but increases tail latency.

kevin_t: Patch notes (local):
```
- Ensure page_release() called on all exit paths in fused_qkv_kernel
- Add page_table sanity check during evict (CRASH if mapping mismatch)
- Add unit test: long_context_kv_paging (runs 50k tokens synthetic)
```

maria_g: Nice. Can you open an issue + PR? We'll need: minimal repro script, failing logs, bisect commit, and tests that run in CI smoke (shorter tokens but same pattern). Also we should run the heavy repro on both H100 and A100 images to validate.

ian_k: Opening issue now and attaching logs. For the H100/A100 runs I noticed slight differences: H100 tends to return stale content (silent corruption) while A100 more often crashes/OOMs. Might be driver timing differences.

ellie_w: Follow-up: adding extra refcount metrics and a small integration test that simulates many small page evicts / reassigns should catch this class of bug. I'll own the test.

perf-bot: Recommendation: add an automated long-context nightly job (once/day) on one H100 and one A100 instance that runs the repro for ~50k tokens to detect regressions early.

maria_g: Action items:
- kevin_t: open PR with the fix + unit test (blocking)
- ellie_w: add integration test + page-refcount metrics (in test infra)
- ian_k: attach full logs + bisect blamelist to the issue and run cross-gpu repros
- infra: schedule nightly long-context job (per perf-bot rec)

kevin_t: Will do PR today. For reviewers, tag runtime and eng-ml.

ian_k: Thanks everyone — marking this thread as the canonical convo for the repro. If you need the raw nvprof traces or kernel dumps I uploaded them to the issue (link in the issue). :thumbsup:
